status: designed before prose; exact new-form IDs and evidence await source/grammar inventory join
headword_input_rule: Print each named dictionary form as visible reference help. An answer token identical to that given form is a reference-position response, even if the same form also has a productive milestone. Assess only independently selected inflections and constructions.

tasks.prompt: Use cniht in its explicitly taught servant sense and bōc book. Translate the four expressions. In each, choose the noun's case from its role rather than from an English word ending.

outputs.label: the servant's book
outputs.target: singular dependent genitive, singular head
outputs.essential_meaning: One servant possesses one book.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not put the head book in genitive merely because its possessor is genitive.

outputs.label: the servants' books
outputs.target: plural dependent genitive and plural head
outputs.essential_meaning: Several servants possess several books.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Distinguish cnihta from cnihtes and the root-noun book plural from an invented regular plural.

outputs.label: I give the servant the book.
outputs.target: singular recipient dative, accusative thing, first-singular giving
outputs.essential_meaning: The speaker gives one book to one servant.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not confuse the servant recipient with the thing given.

outputs.label: We give the servants the books.
outputs.target: plural recipient dative and accusative things, first-plural giving
outputs.essential_meaning: The speakers give several books to several servants.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Change subject agreement, recipient number and book number together.

tasks.prompt: Use the selected endingless accusative of cwēn queen, while retaining its genitive/dative ending. Translate the three expressions, then explain the contrast.

outputs.label: I saw the queen.
outputs.target: endingless accusative singular cwēn
outputs.essential_meaning: The queen is the person seen.
outputs.error_diagnosis: The selected endingless accusative is still accusative; a documented cwēne alternative can be valid but differs from this explicit target.

outputs.label: I gave the queen the book.
outputs.target: dative singular queen as recipient
outputs.essential_meaning: The queen receives the book.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not extend the endingless accusative choice to the dative.

outputs.label: the queen's book
outputs.target: genitive singular dependent plus nominative head
outputs.essential_meaning: A book belonging to the queen.
outputs.error_diagnosis: The same surface as the dative does not establish the same syntactic role.

outputs.label: Explain what the three queen forms show about identifying case from an ending alone.
outputs.target: endingless accusative and genitive/dative syncretism interpreted by construction
outputs.essential_meaning: Case is governed by the whole construction; the selected accusative is endingless, and genitive/dative share an ending.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not infer that an unmarked form must be nominative.

new_dependencies: cwēn complete8cell system with selected accusative and documented variant

tasks.prompt: Use fox fox, hol hole and nest nest. Translate each sentence. Keep ordinary locative on with the dative and distinguish the two neuter plural patterns.

outputs.label: The fox is in the hole.
outputs.target: masculine singular subject and neuter singular locative
outputs.essential_meaning: One fox is located in one hole.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not use an accusative destination phrase for the stated location.

outputs.label: The foxes are in the holes.
outputs.target: plural subject agreement and dative plural location
outputs.essential_meaning: Several foxes are located in several holes.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Change both the subject/verb and the locative phrase to plural.

outputs.label: The nest is in the tree.
outputs.target: neuter singular subject, prior trēo dative singular
outputs.essential_meaning: One nest is located in one tree.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Keep the tree's documented w stem before the ending.

outputs.label: The nests are in the trees.
outputs.target: endingless neuter nominative plural nest and plural copula
outputs.essential_meaning: Several nests are located in several trees.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not infer singular number solely from the unchanged nest surface.

outputs.label: The holes are large.
outputs.target: short-neuter plural holu and plural predicate agreement
outputs.essential_meaning: Several holes are large.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not extend nest's zero plural to short-stem hol or use weak adjective agreement merely because the subject has an article.

tasks.prompt: Use hęrian praise. Supply only the finite form required in each stated setting, then explain the contrast. The dictionary form is visible reference help.

outputs.label: A narrator states: they praise. Give present indicative third plural.
outputs.target: hęrian present indicative third plural
outputs.essential_meaning: An assertion of several people's praising.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not choose the subjunctive wish ending merely because praise is a religious act.

outputs.label: A speaker commands several listeners: praise! Give second-plural imperative.
outputs.target: hęrian second-plural imperative
outputs.essential_meaning: A direct command to several addressees.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Its spelling can match the indicative; identify it by the task's communicative setting.

outputs.label: A speaker wishes: may they praise. Give present subjunctive third plural.
outputs.target: hęrian present subjunctive third plural
outputs.essential_meaning: A third-person wish.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not translate may by a separate permission verb.

outputs.label: Which answers are spelled alike, and what distinguishes their functions?
outputs.target: indicative/imperative syncretism contrasted with subjunctive
outputs.essential_meaning: The present indicative plural and plural imperative share a surface; asserted subject versus commanded addressee and context distinguish them.
outputs.error_diagnosis: A shared spelling does not prove one grammatical analysis.

tasks.prompt: Use the explicitly taught present participles of ondrǣdan fear and hyngran be hungry. Translate the two nominal phrases, then distinguish each phrase's outer case from any object governed inside it.

outputs.label: to those fearing him: use a dative plural participle without an expressed people noun; him is the one feared
outputs.target: outer dative plural nominalized participle with inner accusative person feared
outputs.essential_meaning: The beneficiaries are the people who fear him.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not make the person feared dative simply because the whole participial phrase is dative.

outputs.label: the hungry: give the weak accusative plural phrase used as a direct object
outputs.target: article plus weak accusative plural present participle
outputs.essential_meaning: The hungry people are the direct object.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not restore an unrequested people noun or mistake the phrase for an impersonal finite clause.

outputs.label: State the two grammatical relations in the fear phrase.
outputs.target: dative outer function versus accusative inner government
outputs.essential_meaning: The participle phrase is dative as beneficiary, while ondrǣdan governs the accusative object within it.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Internal dependents do not automatically copy their phrase's outer case.

outputs.label: Explain why a present participle can name people here without being a finite verb.
outputs.target: explicitly taught substantival participle use and inflection
outputs.essential_meaning: The participial form is used nominally for people characterized by the activity or condition; its case follows the noun phrase's role, and no independent finite verb is present.
outputs.error_diagnosis: Do not infer tense/person agreement from the label present participle.

new_dependencies: complete assigned ondrǣdan/hyngran participial display routes
